other_risks: child sexual exploitation and abuse material

mentioned.quote: Risks stemming from possible malicious use of foundation AI models, such as generating content to facilitate cybercrime or child sexual exploitation
mentioned.note: Also the 'Malware code' row of the harms table p.8 ('generate code that could be used to spread malware in a cybercrime').

threshold.note: No cyber level. The harms table (p.7-8) gives an 'illustrative assessment' of likelihood and severity for malware code, not a level that changes what Cohere does. The only gate is generic (no regressions vs previous model, p.16).

response.quote: Any performance regressions identified during any such testing or evaluations, including the final pre-deployment evaluation, are investigated and mitigated before deployment.
response.note: Generic launch gate (E3, read with E1 present tense): p.16 'This is Cohere’s bright line for determining when a model is “acceptable” from a risk management perspective and ready to be launched.' Covers the harms the evaluations target, including malicious-use cybercrime/malware. No cyber threshold, recorded as a gap.

acc_decider.quote: The final authority to determine if our products are safe, secure, and ready to be made available to our customers is delegated by Cohere’s CEO to Cohere’s Chief Scientist.
acc_decider.note: Decides whether to proceed under the generic gate that covers this risk.

acc_external.note: Third-party penetration testing of containers (p.10, p.16) tests Cohere's own system security, not safeguards against offensive cyber misuse; red teaming 'may include independent external parties' (p.16) is hedged.

acc_unmet.note: Only the generic no-regression gate (p.16), which E4 excludes; nothing says what happens if a required named response cannot be met.

mentioned.note: Biorisk appears only in the boxed description of 'One approach to risk assurance in the AI industry' (p.14-15, E7) and in a critique that existing biorisk research 'fails to account' for risk chains (p.15); Cohere's own approach is 'focused on risks that are known, measurable, or observable today' (p.15).
